pr_title: sql: fix cast from int to char by interpreting integer as ASCII byte
pr_body:
Fixes: #70771 

Release note (sql change): Earlier the behavior of casting an int
to "char" was similar to bpchar where we returned only
the first digit of the integer. Now, we are interpreting
int cast to "char" as an ASCII byte to align the overall
behavior more with PostgreSQL.

Release note (sql change): A parameter of type "char" can now be used as
a parameter in a prepared statement.

This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/70942)

It looks like there is a special case for `0` too: 

```
marcus=# select i, i::"char", length(i::"char"), i::"char" = ' '::"char" from (values (97), (127), (0), (-1), (-127), (-128)) v(i);
  i   |  i   | length | ?column?
------+------+--------+----------
   97 | a    |      1 | f
  127 | \x7F |      1 | f
    0 |      |      0 | f
   -1 |      |      1 | f
 -127 |      |      1 | f
 -128 |      |      1 | f
(6 rows)
```

Postgres's code for casting an integer to a `"char"` is here: https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/b484ddf4d2eb81736512efa35ed3e5d2a72993d8/src/backend/utils/adt/char.c#L161-L172

Where `SCHAR_MIN` is -128 and `SCHAR_MAX` is 127.

You'll have to specially handle the `0::"char"` case to return an empty string to match the behavior of null-terminated strings.

@mgartner yes, I have made relevant changes to handle edge cases. I am little unsure about the PostgreSQL interpretation of `0::"char"` though.
```
postgres=# select 0::"char";
 char
------

(1 row)

postgres=# select 32::"char";
 char
------

(1 row)
```
both 0 and 32 returns the same result. Let me know your thoughts regarding this? Thanks!

they actually aren't the same, but it's hard to tell because it's whitespace:
```
rafiss@127:postgres> select i, i::"char", length(i::"char"), i::"char" = ' '::"char" from (values (97), (127), (0), (32)) v(i);
+-----+-----+----------+------------+
| i   | i   | length   | ?column?   |
|-----+-----+----------+------------|
| 97  | a   | 1        | False      |
| 127 |      | 1        | False      |
| 0   |     | 0        | False      |
| 32  |     | 1        | True       |
+-----+-----+----------+------------+
```

i'd recommend adding this `select i, i::"char", length(i::"char"), i::"char" = ' '::"char" from (values (97), (127), (0), (32)) v(i);` query as a test case in `pkg/sql/logictest/testdata/logic_test/cast` so that this is easier to assert on. (and also include more values in that `values` clause too.)

---

although @mgartner i get different behavior than you for negative numbers:
```
rafiss@127:postgres> select i, i::"char", length(i::"char"), i::"char" = ' '::"char" from (values (-1)) v(i);
'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 0: invalid start byte
```

maybe an ASCII vs UTF8 thing

update: the difference with negative numbers was client side. i was testing with `pgcli`. if i test with `psql` my results match @mgartner 

so let's add this test case to a logic test, as well as some out of range cases

```
rafiss=# select i, i::"char", length(i::"char"), i::"char" = ' '::"char" from (values (32), (97), (127), (0), (-1), (-127), (-128)) v(i);

------+------+--------+----------

    0 |      |      0 | f

(7 rows)

rafiss=# select 128::"char";
ERROR:  "char" out of range

rafiss=# select (-129)::"char";
ERROR:  "char" out of range
```

issue_context.title: sql: cast from integer to "char" should interpret the integer as an ASCII byte
issue_context.body:
In Postgres:

```
marcus=# SELECT 97::"char";
 char
------
 a
(1 row)

marcus=# SELECT 128::"char";
ERROR:  22003: "char" out of range
```

In CockroachDB v21.2.x:

```
demo@127.0.0.1:26257/defaultdb> SELECT 97::"char";
  char
-------
    9
(1 row)

demo@127.0.0.1:26257/defaultdb> SELECT 128::"char";
  char
-------
   1
(1 row)
```
comments: Hey @mgartner @rafiss, Can I work on this if no one's working on this?

Absolutely. You'll probably be making changes somewhere in `pkg/sql/sem/tree/casts.go` and you can add tests in `pkg/sql/sem/tree/testdata/eval/cast`. You can see that I highlight the problem with some tests and `TODO`s in [#70722](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/70722/files#diff-f49548b6dfcc1484442b5fa07fad85974d900a751278845a85be198e5133aea4R1279). You can add similar tests.

Let me know if you have any questions.

@mgartner Hi, I was looking into the current implementation and it looks like we cast the same way for both `char` and `text` types. Since Postgres processes the 2 types differently this change could break some of the existing test cases.

```
postgres=# select length(123::text);
 length
--------
      3
(1 row)

postgres=# select length(123::char);
 length
--------
      1
(1 row)
```

what are your thoughts on this?
We should match Postgres's behavior. `97::TEXT` should result in `'97'` and `97::"char"` should result in `'a'`. Which test cases would this break?
@mgartner my bad! I got confused with the text and char types. Thanks for clarifying! 🙇🏼
